$comment: Quantities that more than one component computes. Each row names the two producers and
the test that asserts they agree. A quantity with two producers and no agreement test is
a defect waiting for one of them to change alone; this project has met that failure three
times, and every one of them was a guard applied to one of two symmetric channels.
Checked mechanically by .github/scripts/assurance/relational_pairs.py: producers are named
by SYMBOL and must still exist in src/; a named test must still exist in test/.
A row with status 'open' is a pair we have not yet tied together. Publishing the count
rather than hiding it is the point: a register that only lists solved rows measures

pairs.note: The floor the planner attests must equal the floor the executor enforces, for split and multi-hop shapes alike.
Previewed net output against realised delivery when a route input is a registered bridge.
The same parity where no route input is a bridge and the fee is charged per hop. This row was open until the preview was taught the regime.
What the planner is allowed to compose must be executable; an executor cap below the planner budget turns a valid plan into a revert.
The library's quote for the stable curve against what the executor delivers through the venue.
Depth as the library computes it against depth as the registry stores it, per venue family.

The registry is handed what the hop was able to spend, not what the route declared. The ratio of measured to declared is uniform across the legs of a hop, so one word per hop reconstructs each leg's real spend exactly - which is what let this be tied without widening a call frame already at the via-ir stack limit.
